title: فِعْل التَّعَجُّب, the Vocative يَا with a مُضَاف, and the Rules for Numbers 21–30
summary: Reading through lesson nine's passage on the creation of the sun, moon, stars and seas, the class picks up فِعْل التَّعَجُّب — the pattern مَا أَفْعَلَ for expressing amazement — and the rule that a noun after يَا takes a ḍamma unless it is a مُضَاف, in which case it takes a fatḥa. Lesson ten then formally introduces the مُضَارِع and sets out the numbers from twenty-one upward, where the tens stay fixed and only the unit flips gender, apart from one and two.
key_points: فِعْل التَّعَجُّب (fiʿl al-taʿajjub : the verb of amazement) turns a plain statement into an exclamation on the pattern مَا أَفْعَلَ: هَذَا الدَّرْسُ سَهْلٌ becomes مَا أَسْهَلَ هَذَا الدَّرْسَ — how easy this lesson is. Both the أَفْعَل word and the thing marvelled at take a fatḥa.

After يَا, a single noun takes a ḍamma — يَا رَجُلُ، يَا أُسْتَاذُ، يَا رَحْمَانُ. But if what follows is a مُضَاف, the first word takes a fatḥa instead: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ، يَا أَبَا بَكْرٍ.
A plural of something غَيْر عَاقِل is treated grammatically as a feminine singular — نُجُوم is referred to with خَلَقَهَا — yet it is still translated as a plural, Allah created them.

Some nouns are feminine without carrying any feminine marker: شَمْس (sun), نَار (fire), جَهَنَّم, and نَفْس. This is why the answer to مَنْ خَلَقَ الشَّمْسَ is خَلَقَهَا اللَّهُ with a feminine pronoun.

جَمْع مُؤَنَّث سَالِم — the sound feminine plural on the ـَات pattern, such as سَمَاوَات، مُسْلِمَات، طَالِبَات، سَيَّارَات — cannot take a fatḥa; where one is due it becomes a kasra, as in خَلَقَ اللَّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ and إِنَّ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَالْمُسْلِمَاتِ.

A pronoun suffixed to a verb changes who is acted upon: خَلَقَ is simply created, while خَلَقَكَ is created you — so مَنْ خَلَقَكَ needs the كَ, whereas مَنْ خَلَقَ السَّمَاءَ names its object separately.
The مُضَارِع can express an action happening now, one in the future, or a general habit; only the context of the sentence decides which — يَذْهَبُ إِلَى السُّوقِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ is habitual.
The vowel on the third letter of the مُضَارِع varies by word — يَذْهَبُ carries a fatḥa while يَغْسِلُ carries a kasra — and must be learned per verb.
For 21 to 30 and the same decades beyond, the tens word stays unchanged (عِشْرُونَ، ثَلَاثُونَ، أَرْبَعُونَ) and only the unit is adjusted for gender, taking the opposite gender to the مَعْدُود.
One and two are the exception: there the عَدَد matches the مَعْدُود — وَاحِدٌ وَعِشْرُونَ طَالِبًا against إِحْدَى وَعِشْرُونَ طَالِبَةً.
In this range the مَعْدُود is singular and takes a fatḥa; the tens word itself changes ending after a preposition, as in ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى سِتَّةٍ وَعِشْرِينَ طَالِبًا.
Telling the time uses إِلَّا for the remainder — التَّاسِعَةُ إِلَّا رُبْعًا is a quarter to nine, that is 8:45 — and النِّصْف for the half hour.

Vocabulary: عَادَ (to return), جَدّ (grandfather), الْعَاصِمَة (capital city) with الْخُرْطُوم as Sudan's, طِين (clay) as تُرَاب mixed with water, مُخْتَلِط (mixed), رَفَعَ (to raise) with يَد as its object, قَائِمَة (list), لَحْظَة (a moment, very common in speech), أَحْيَانًا (sometimes), مُتَأَخِّرًا (late) against مُبَكِّرًا (early), and صَحِيفَة with its plural صُحُف (newspapers).
عَلَاقَة in Arabic means a connection or relation, not an area as the similar word does in Urdu.
اسْم التَّفْضِيل again: بَعِيد (far) gives أَبْعَد (farther), used for the stars being farther than the sun.
questions: [00:03:00] Q: Is it the مَا that makes it a فِعْل التَّعَجُّب, or the whole construction? — A: The أَفْعَل word is itself the verb of amazement; مَا together with the fatḥa on what follows is the format it takes.
[00:06:00] Q: Does جَدّ mean grandfather or grandmother? — A: Grandfather, from either the mother's or the father's side.
[00:09:00] Q: Is الْبِحَار the plural of بَحْر, or the other way round? — A: الْبِحَار is the plural of بَحْر.
[00:11:00] Q: Why is the pronoun in خَلَقَهَا feminine when asked about الشَّمْس? — A: Because شَمْس is one of the words that are feminine without any feminine marker, like نَار، جَهَنَّم and نَفْس.
[00:14:00] Q: Is نُجُوم feminine or masculine? — A: Masculine, but it is غَيْر عَاقِل and plural, so it is treated grammatically as a feminine singular while still being translated as a plural.
[00:15:01] Q: Does عَلَاقَة mean area, as the similar word does in Urdu? — A: No — in Arabic it means a connection or relation.
[00:18:00] Q: Why does السَّمَاوَات not take a fatḥa when it is the object of خَلَقَ? — A: Because it is جَمْع مُؤَنَّث سَالِم on the ـَات pattern, and such plurals take a kasra where a fatḥa is due.
[00:20:02] Q: What is the extra قَاف — sorry, كَاف — in خَلَقَكَ? — A: It is not part of the verb; it is the ضَمِير meaning you, so the phrase means who created you.
[00:37:00] Q: Does the tens word change its ending? — A: Yes, after a preposition it does: إِلَى سِتَّةٍ وَعِشْرِينَ takes the kasra form.

quiz.q: How would you turn هَذَا الدَّرْسُ سَهْلٌ into an expression of amazement?
quiz.a: فِعْل التَّعَجُّب follows مَا أَفْعَلَ with a fatḥa on both the أَفْعَل word and the thing marvelled at.

quiz.q: What ending does a single noun take after يَا?
quiz.a: يَا رَجُلُ، يَا أُسْتَاذُ — a ḍamma, unless the noun is a مُضَاف.

quiz.q: Why is it يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ with a fatḥa rather than يَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ?
options: Because it is a proper name
Because عَبْد is a مُضَاف to اللَّهِ
Because it is being addressed in the plural
quiz.a: The exception to the ḍamma rule: when what follows يَا is a مُضَاف, the first word takes a fatḥa — يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ, يَا أُخْتَ هَارُونَ.

quiz.q: Which of these is feminine despite having no feminine marker?
quiz.a: شَمْس is feminine, as are نَار، جَهَنَّم and نَفْس — which is why the answer was خَلَقَهَا اللَّهُ.

quiz.q: How is a plural of something غَيْر عَاقِل treated grammatically?
quiz.a: النُّجُوم takes خَلَقَهَا, though it is still translated as a plural — Allah created them.

quiz.q: In the range 21 to 29, which part of the number changes for gender?
options: The unit, and it takes the opposite gender to the مَعْدُود
quiz.a: عِشْرُونَ stays fixed while the unit flips against the gender of the counted noun.

quiz.q: Which numbers are the exception, matching the gender of the مَعْدُود?
quiz.a: وَاحِدٌ وَعِشْرُونَ طَالِبًا but إِحْدَى وَعِشْرُونَ طَالِبَةً — one and two agree rather than oppose.

quiz.q: What form does the مَعْدُود take with 21 to 30?
quiz.a: The counted noun stays singular and carries a fatḥa — طَالِبًا, not طُلَّابًا.

quiz.q: What time is التَّاسِعَةُ إِلَّا رُبْعًا?
quiz.a: إِلَّا subtracts, so it is a quarter to nine — the teacher compared it to the British quarter to habit.
Flagged as very common in spoken Arabic: لَحْظَة يَا أَخِي means just one moment.

quran_examples.arabic: قَالَ أَنَا خَيْرٌ مِّنْهُ خَلَقْتَنِي مِن نَّارٍ وَخَلَقْتَهُ مِن طِينٍ
quran_examples.transliteration: qāla anā khayrun minhu khalaqtanī min nārin wa-khalaqtahu min ṭīn
quran_examples.translation: He said: I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay.
quran_examples.note: A student's answer for how the jinn were created, cited from Sūrat al-Aʿrāf; it also shows خَلَقْتَنِي and خَلَقْتَهُ with the attached pronouns the class had just been parsing.

quran_examples.arabic: إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ
quran_examples.transliteration: inna rabbakumu llāhu alladhī khalaqa al-samāwāti wa-l-arḍa fī sittati ayyām
quran_examples.translation: Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days.
quran_examples.note: The passage the lesson's dialogue drew on, and السَّمَاوَاتِ in it is the very example of a جَمْع مُؤَنَّث سَالِم object taking a kasra instead of a fatḥa.

quran_examples.arabic: إِنَّ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَالْمُسْلِمَاتِ وَالْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ وَالْقَانِتِينَ وَالْقَانِتَاتِ
quran_examples.transliteration: inna al-muslimīna wa-l-muslimāti wa-l-muʾminīna wa-l-muʾmināti wa-l-qānitīna wa-l-qānitāt
quran_examples.translation: Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women, the obedient men and obedient women…
quran_examples.note: The teacher's own example: إِنَّ should give a fatḥa, yet every ـَات plural here takes a kasra, while the مُذَكَّر سَالِم plurals beside them take the yāʾ form.

quran_examples.arabic: يَا أُخْتَ هَارُونَ مَا كَانَ أَبُوكِ امْرَأَ سَوْءٍ وَمَا كَانَتْ أُمُّكِ بَغِيًّا
quran_examples.transliteration: yā ukhta hārūna mā kāna abūki mraʾa sawʾin wa-mā kānat ummuki baghiyyā
quran_examples.translation: O sister of Hārūn, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste.
quran_examples.note: The teacher's Qur'ānic case of يَا followed by a مُضَاف taking a fatḥa — أُخْتَ rather than أُخْتُ.

quran_examples.translation: It is He who created seven heavens in layers.
quran_examples.note: Matches the dialogue's سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ, showing a counted noun after a number from three to ten taking the plural, in contrast to the singular required from eleven upward.
